main_text.p: ,, and legacies bestowed vpon the Church, be for the mainetenance of pietie andtrue religion, and to good vses, not to nourish idolatrie and superstition: or if they bee giuen through ignorace of the time,to such vnlawfull purposes, they ought by the Prince to bee converted to better and more godly vses: As now in England,the lands of Colleges,which were first giuen to maintaine that abominable Idoll of theMasse,are turned to the maintenace of learning and true religion. So was the lawe of Moses, that the gold, and siluer, brasse yron, tinne, lead, which the Israelites should receiue of the heathen, first should passe through the fire, & so be made cleane,and fit for holy vses.Adducitque eum in finem argumentum ad hominem,quod ipsi Papistæ annuunt aliquando ut quædam ipsorum in meliores usus convertantur. Concil. Colonienf. part 9. cap 9. cap.21. Fraternitates, quæ vocantur, & in honorem aliquorum sanctorum in ecclesiis fiunt,/speciem quidem pietatis habent, sed quales hae tempestate seruantur, & in quibus tam Clerici, quam laici potissimum comessationibus & ebrietatibus vacant, interdum etiam variis conspirationibus aduersus potestates intenti sunt, sublatas malumus, & redditus in usus pauperum expendi. Idem, Comment.in Exod. xx. ad viii. praecept. ad sacrilegium refert: when the church goods are imployed to another end, than for the which they were first giue the Church: which was to maintaine the ministerie of the word of God and Sacraments, to relieve the pore,to maintaine the edifices of the Church.Let such therefore looke unto it,as live of the tithes and revenues of the Church, being lay men,not called to the office of teaching,instructing and spirituall feeding.Similiter Iohannes Weemle of Lathocker, Scotus,in Expofit.Caeremoniali ad praecept. viii. exercit. xxxi. There was never one that medled with those holy things,to devoure them, or turne them to their owne private use and commodity, but it was a snare to him:Iehoiakim tooke the Cedar out of the house of God &c. Georgius Downaus,in Summ Officiorum

page.notes: Lower right corner watermark "Digitized by Google" is a digitiser's mark and omitted. The final word "rum" is the end of "Officiorum", set on its own line at the right.
